title: What Does an AI Engineer Do Now? - Aparna Dhinakaran, Arize AI
talk_summary: Arize's Aparna Dhinakaran describes building 'Signal', an always-on agent that reads telemetry traces, identifies issues, and opens PRs, and argues the AI engineer's job is now building the loop (triggers, sandboxes, memory, evals) rather than individual features. The concrete mechanisms are durable sandboxed runs with externalized state, persistent issue memory across runs, and evaluating the evaluators against human judgment.

takeaways.technique: Durable runs with externalized state and resumable sandboxes
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent run spins up a fresh sandbox loaded with context; state is saved outside the sandbox so a failed harness or sandbox can be relaunched and resume from the failed step rather than restarting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the sandbox fails, or if the harness fails, then it shouldn't have to start everything from scratch in the middle of the run

takeaways.what_they_do: Outputs of each run (issues found) are saved to memory so the next run knows what was already seen and can escalate issues that recur, instead of starting from zero.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it doesn't have to start from ground zero. It has a history of what are the issues that it actually found

takeaways.technique: Evaluate the evaluators against golden human-labeled data
takeaways.what_they_do: They build golden-truth datasets, run the evaluator, compare to human output, and only ship the evaluator once judge-human agreement is established; evals run both offline and online.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually evaluate the evaluators ... verify them against the human output, and then try to align

takeaways.what_they_do: Signal runs on multiple harnesses (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and multiple models so they can measure whether cheaper models maintain issue-detection quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: can we reduce the cost and actually still maintain the rigor um and maintain the quality of issues that are actually detected

takeaways.technique: Single-proxy sandbox with full tracing and credential teardown
takeaways.what_they_do: All context, repo access, and keys go into a sandbox; the only ingress/egress is one proxy, everything inside is traced, and credentials/repo access are torn down after each run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the only way to get information in and out of the sandbox is by this single proxy, and everything that happens inside of that sandbox is actually already getting traced

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents wake on configurable cadence (every 3-6 hours), events (Slack complaints), or metric thresholds, rather than waiting for human assignment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's configurable to run on an ongoing cadence. So, every 3 hours, 6 hours ... It can also be triggered by events
